gap: No result ChatGPT got states that BLUETTI connects the AC180's add-on batteries (B80, B230 and B300) only through its DC7909 port with a separate cable ($29.90 for the B80, $89 for the B230/B300), and that BLUETTI calls the battery's role 'Power Bank mode', so the AC180 is not expandable the way the AC200L is.
standout_why: Of the two cited pages, OutdoorGearLab's AC180 review lists 'optional expansion batteries' and says the unit 'allows you to increase battery capacity as your power needs grow'. It names no battery, cable or mode. preparedstates.com (#14) shows the AC180 as expandable 'To 4,224Wh' with no battery model or cable. The cited CNET/Yahoo piece returned 403, so I could not check it. ChatGPT's answer says the Elite 200 V2 lacks direct expansion but says nothing about how the AC180 connects to a battery. None of these pages names the DC7909 cables or BLUETTI's 'Power Bank mode' wording. None notes that the Elite 100 V2 ships with only an AC cable, which Notebookcheck says leaves out a solar or car cable. None names the Elite 200 V2's XT60 PV input rated to 25 A.
decides: This backs the Elite 100 V2 over the AC180. The AC180's main selling point on rival pages, expandability, works only as an external battery feeding a DC7909 port, through cables BLUETTI sells separately. Both cost $499 on bluettipower.com today, and the AC180 is out of stock until late November. It does not change the Elite 200 V2 pick. Shoppers who need real expansion should go to the Apex 300 (B300K) or AC200L.

findings.label: B80 battery hookup: cable and mode
findings.value: B80 Aviation-plug to DC7909 cable, $29.90. BLUETTI says the B80 runs in 'Power Bank mode' when connected to the AC180
findings.note: Maker's product text, read through storecheck: 'B80-AVIATION PLUG TO DC7909: Need more power for your EB3A, EB70, EB70S, or AC180? ... keep your devices running longer while the B80 is in Power Bank mode.'

findings.label: B230 / B300 battery hookup: cable
findings.value: P090D to DC7909 cable, $89.00, 59 in / 150 cm. Applicable models: EB150, EB240, AC180
findings.note: The same page lists P090D to Aviation ($99) for the AC200L. It says standalone output at the P090D port of a B230/B300 is turned on by holding the power button for about 10 s. The page names no Elite V2 model.

findings.label: B230 page's own compatibility list (US store)
findings.value: Lists 'AC200Max (Original Expansion), AC200P/EB150/EB240 (DC-DC Connection via D050S)'. The AC180 is not on the list
findings.note: The page shows $999 (was $1,299). Its markup includes Discontinued, Out of Stock and Pre-Order labels, so availability is unclear.

findings.label: US price and stock
findings.value: $499.00, out of stock, expected restock late November (page also says 'ships from 12.14')
findings.note: The two dates on the page conflict. Solar input is listed only as '500W Max'.

findings.label: Solar / DC input
findings.value: 1,000 W max, 12–60 V, 20 A max. AC + DC dual charging up to 1,200 W
findings.source_title: BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 Portable Power Station | 1,800W 1,024Wh
findings.note: From the page's compare table. The page lists one AC charging cable in the box. It says 'Recharge via BLUETTI Charger 1 while driving.' Price $499.00.

findings.label: Charger 1 alternator charger bundle price
findings.note: Read through storecheck. The Charger 1 page (https://www.bluettipower.com/products/bluetti-charger-1) says it 'Works with all BLUETTI power stations', is rated at 560 W max, and includes a DC input cable and an MC4 output cable.

findings.label: Route to a B300K battery
findings.value: BLUETTI sells it only as a bundle with Charger 2 and DC Hub (Elite 100 V2 + B300K + Charger 2 + DC Hub), $2,199.00
findings.source_title: Elite 100 V2 + B300K + Charger 2+ DC Hub
findings.note: Bundle title and price only. The Charger 2 page (https://www.bluettipower.com/products/bluetti-charger-2-alternator-solar-charger) does not say whether a B300K can charge the Elite 100 V2. It lists 1,200 W total, 800 W alternator and 600 W solar.

findings.label: PV input connector and parallel-panel cable
findings.value: XT60 PV input, solar input current up to 25 A. Two panels in parallel need the XT60-to-dual-MC4 cable ($49, 12 AWG, 25 A), currently not available
findings.source_title: BLUETTI XT60 to MC4 Solar Parallel Cable
findings.note: The page says the cable is 'Designed for BLUETTI power stations with an XT60 PV input and up to 25 A solar input current, including Elite 200 V2, Apex 300, Elite 300, Elite 320, Elite 400'. The Elite 100 V2 is not named, and its own page gives a 20 A input max.

findings.label: Maker's compatibility statement
findings.value: MC4 connector. BLUETTI says it works 'As long as the power station has MC4 connectors and voltage specs compatible with BLUETTI solar panels'. No model list. Price $849.00
findings.note: The Tech Specs section on the page is empty, so I could not check Voc against the 12–60 V inputs. BLUETTI sells SORA 500 bundles only with the Elite 300, Elite 400 and Apex 300.
